profile.address: 171 MLK Student Union, UC Berkeley, Berkeley, CA
profile.reading:
The Open Computing Facility, known as the OCF, is an all volunteer student organization at the University of California, Berkeley, not a commercial data center. Its computer lab occupies room 171 in the Martin Luther King Jr. Student Union building on the Berkeley campus in Alameda County, California. A copyright notice on the organization's own site spans 1989 to the present, which this page treats as evidence the group has operated continuously since 1989, making it one of the longer running student run computing organizations in the country.

The OCF provides free shell accounts, web and email hosting for student groups and individuals, printing services, and a GPU server used for coursework and personal projects, all staffed and maintained by student volunteers rather than paid professional operations staff. Its infrastructure lives in a campus server room rather than a purpose built data center, and the organization does not publish square footage, power capacity, cooling design, uptime commitments or any of the specifications typically associated with commercial or enterprise data center facilities, because none of those concepts apply to a small student run server room in the way they do to a colocation or hyperscale site.

This page describes the OCF honestly as a campus computing club rather than a commercial facility, and no capacity or power figures are reported here because the operator does not publish any and none are appropriate to estimate for a room of this kind.
